## What landed

### The driver-owned routing seam (ADR-0338 D1–D2)

`hh-control::driver` gains `RoutingPort` + `ResponseCachePort` and the
`RoutingLane`/`CacheBinding` data records. The bound `router` slot's
lane declares role, capability axes, budget, and the realized
`RoutingPolicy` + `ModelRoleTable`; the port owns the views
(`SelectorView`, `BudgetPort`, health/C1 views) and computes; the
driver owns ordering and every durable append through the fenced
writer. Consult side rows (`control.budget.{reserved,released}`,
`model.profile.status.changed`) drain through
`RoutingPort::take_rows` — the `AssembleOutcome.side_events`
convention (CC3 durable-before-visible).

Emission order on a routed run: `model.route.decided` lands before the
call scope opens (ahead of the `model.call.requested` it binds);
`model.call.attempt.{started,completed,failed}` mint per attempt; a
failed attempt runs the ADR-0122 consult over `error_actions` —
`Retry` restarts on the same target, `Reroute` emits
`model.surface.relowered` (cross-profile) → `model.rerouted` → the
restarted `attempt.started` (`check_reroute_order`'s sequence),
`GiveUp` closes the call; a select refusal lands a typed
`control.guard.fired` row and closes `select_refused` — never a silent
skip or a fabricated target.

Routing state — the `attempted` set, per-target attempt counts, the
reroute count, the pending-fresh-decision flag — is rebuilt by folding
`model.route.decided`/`model.rerouted`/`attempt.*` over the durable
prefix (D2); resume/takeover re-arms the lane with no session memory
involved. With no port wired the scripted lane is byte-identical —
`r2_7_unbound_lane_is_byte_identical` pins the asymmetry as declared,
not silent.

### The codec half (D3)

`RoutingPolicy::from_json` and `RoutingDecision::from_json` — strict
inverse codecs for the existing emitters: required members enforced,
`content_hash` computed when absent, unknown `kind`/`error_actions`
spellings refused. The conditioned-rule `debt` member decodes through
`hh_compiler::schema::debt_from_json` (now `pub`) — the event-payload
helper dropped the additive members (`removal_test`, `reach_via`,
`debt_class`, `hypothesis_typed`, `scope`, `expiry`, `runway_ms`,
`revalidation`, `created_at`, `supersedes`); CC1 — one codec per
record.

### The offline-decidable arm cut (D4)

`static`, `role_table`, `fallback_chain`, `capability_filter` select
over the realized `ModelRoleTable` alone. `cost_cap` selects under a
declared pricing view and answers a typed refusal without one
(`r2_7_cost_cap_without_pricing_refuses`). `learned` refuses unless
its evolution-evidence binding is present
(`r2_7_learned_policy_refuses_offline`). Live-signal members (live
health, price discovery) produce the closed `RoutingRefusal` spellings
— a missing view is never coerced to healthy/zero/available.

### Kernel-side arm (hh-embed; D5–D7)

`KernelRouting`/`KernelK5`/`StaticProfiles`/`KernelBudget` arm the
bound slot: the realized role table resolves through
`RegistryProfiles`'s new `SelectorView` impl (`registered()`
enumeration — profile selection sees every registered profile);
declared `probes[]` mint `model.profile.probed` durable before the
first call (+ `model.profile.status.changed{trigger: probe}` when a
probe record contradicts the declared status); the `response_cache`
slot binds `KernelK5` over `hh_context::k5` — one
`model.cache.resolved` per lookup scoped to its call. `model_fail[]`
stages call outcomes (`StagedCall::Fail{class, retry_after_ms?}` |
`Pass`) as process staging — a drained plan means success, nothing
fabricates a failure; a durable resume re-arms the script whole from
the lane declaration. Router slot params use the identity-safe
`candidate` spelling — `model_ref`/`version` inside a semantic
projection trip T-LCD-01 (D7). A malformed slot refuses open
(`r2_7_malformed_router_slot_refuses_open`).

New ledger classes registered in `hh-ledger` (CC10): the model-plane
`model.*` classes the driver mints, including
`model.profile.status.changed` and `model.profile.probed`.

### WireDialect codec leg (R-2.3.1)

The AC-R-2.3.1-2 golden corpus (13 shapes × 2 provider-faithful
families) landed at S3.7
(`golden_corpus_thirteen_shapes_two_families`); R2.7's cell pins the
codec path in-battery — both family documents round-trip through
`WireDialect::to_json`/`from_json` verbatim, `content_id` is
round-trip-stable, and an unknown member refuses
(`r2_7_dialect_documents_codec_round_trip`).
